reasons.runs-where-asked: The call runs in the scope it was asked in (the Team turn's, its asker's login), met with its asker's rights now. On main it ran with no scope at all on the web, Telegram and batch paths (the system pool, as its asker's login), and in the approver's own scope over MCP, where a Team connector is not held and the Team note is not read, so the owner's MCP approval was claimed and then failed at run. Since fix round 1 the owner's MCP approval reads the row on the system pool, so it is judged and runs where it was asked too.
reasons.gains-not-the-calls: Rights the asker gained after asking (a Moderator seat elsewhere, Admin's) are not the call's: it runs in the scope it was asked in, never wider. On main it ran unscoped, or in the approver's MCP scope (the owner's, where it was claimed and then failed at run).
reasons.lost-workspace: The asker left the workspace it asked in: the approval is refused before the claim (an ApprovalRefusedError, 403 on the web, an error over MCP) and the call stays pending, run nowhere. On main it ran unscoped as its asker, or over MCP was claimed in the approver's scope and failed at run. Since fix round 1 this holds over MCP too: the row is read on the system pool, where the approver's own scope (its own MCP, an asker that left) would read nothing.
reasons.lost-moderator: The asker lost its Moderator seat where it asked: the queue-time check run again refuses it (the connector's write rule; the item rule for the note), before the claim, and the call stays pending. On main it ran unscoped, or was claimed and then failed at run (over MCP, in the approver's scope).
reasons.lost-item: What the call names is no longer the asked scope's (the note homed in another workspace, the connector no longer a resource of the workspace): the item pre-check (since the pre-check removal: the tool's precondition, which no longer finds the note in the scope) or the connector rule refuses it again before the claim, and it stays pending. On main it ran unscoped, or was claimed and then failed at run (over MCP, in the approver's scope).
reasons.pre-check-removal: note_update's item pre-check went (docs/actors.md, "Pre-check deletion"): the database refuses the write itself, with both checks on, in the scope the call was asked in. A call queued by a member who may not edit the note is no longer refused before it is queued, and a call whose asker lost its Moderator seat is no longer held back before the claim: each is claimed and run where it was asked, and the database refuses it ('approved' with the database's words as its error; the note unchanged). A plain member's queued call meets each approver's own rule as any call does (an approver that may not approve it, or does not see it, leaves it pending). Nothing is written in any of these cells.
